p: Here's a cracking bit of trivia: the man who designed Castle Howard, Sir John Vanbrugh, was best known as a playwright and had never designed a building before. With the help of Nicholas Hawksmoor, he created this showstopper for Charles Howard, 3rd Earl of Carlisle, with work starting at the very end of the seventeenth century. Not a bad first attempt. In 1940 a fire badly damaged the house and destroyed the great dome, which was later rebuilt, so look up and appreciate the restoration work.
Telly fans will know it from more than Brideshead. It also played Clyvedon, the Bridgerton family's country home, in the Netflix series, and spotting familiar corners is a fun game for the grown-ups.

Out in the grounds, a few landmarks are worth the walk. The Atlas Fountain sits in front of the house, the Temple of the Four Winds gazes over the landscape, and Hawksmoor's Mausoleum stands on a distant rise, a grand and slightly eerie sight. Ray Wood, behind the house, has woodland paths through rhododendrons and rare trees.

Allow most of a day; this isn't a place to rush. Afterwards, the market town of Malton is only a few miles away and has built a big reputation for food, with independent producers, bakeries and a monthly food market. Kirkham Priory, a ruined medieval abbey beside the River Derwent, is another peaceful stop on the way back to York.
